title: Context Window Budget
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Artificial Intelligence
Large Language Models
Context Window
Token Budgets
description: Check items on and off to spend an example 50,000-token context window. Each item stacks into a vertical bar as a colored segment; when the total passes the window limit, the part above the limit turns red and a message says the model cannot see it. All token sizes are example values, not measurements.

educational.topic: Context window limits in large language models
learningObjectives: Demonstrate why content beyond a model's context-window limit becomes unavailable to it.
Calculate the total tokens used by a combination of files and compare it with a window limit.
Identify which loaded item causes a context window to overflow.
prerequisites: Has read the definition of a context window

equations: total = sum of tokens for every checked item
assumptions: The 50,000-token window is an example size; real windows vary by model
Item token sizes are example values, not measurements of real files
Items stack in a fixed order, so the last item in the stack is the one cut off
limitations: Does not model how a specific tool truncates or summarizes an oversized session
Does not model the tokens used by the model's own reply

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner combines values and observes the consequence (overflow) rather than watching a fixed demonstration
keyQuestions: What happens to content that lands past the window limit?
Which item grows during a session even when no new files are loaded?
commonMisconceptions: A model can still partly remember content that no longer fits in its context window
Only files count against the window; the conversation itself is free
assessmentOpportunities: Choose one change that brings an overflowing window back under the limit and justify it
